LanguageData.VTU_RestartNote: Turn each fix or tweak on or off. Changes take effect after restarting the game.
LanguageData.VTU_RestartRequired: Restart the game to apply this change.
LanguageData.VTU_Failed: Could not be applied (see the log); this module is off for this session.
LanguageData.VTU_ProvidedByLegacy: (skipped: already provided by the standalone mod "{0}")
LanguageData.VTU_FactionLeader_Desc: Fixes the "Faction leader for X is null" error by generating a new leader the way vanilla does when a leader dies.
LanguageData.VTU_HistoryGraph_Desc: Removes the History tab lag in long-running colonies. The graph looks the same; peaks and dips stay visible.
LanguageData.VTU_RightClickMenu_Desc: Stops the stutter when a right-click menu opens and while it is open on the map. Options are generated once on opening instead of three times, re-checked every 5 seconds instead of every 4th frame, and still on click.
LanguageData.VTU_TradeDeal_Desc: Removes the long freeze when a trade window opens in a colony with many items. With Auto Seller, its trades no longer rebuild the trade list a second time.
LanguageData.VTU_SiegeBuilder_Desc: Fixes the error spam when a sieging group contains mechs (added by other mods): pawns without skills defend the camp instead of building it.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerFoodPolicy_Desc: Wardens no longer bring restricted food to a prisoner having a mental break. A pawn in a mental break that feeds itself behaves as in vanilla.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerBleeding: Tend or operate on prisoners before feeding
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerBleeding_Desc: Wardens skip feeding and food delivery while a prisoner is still bleeding or has surgery scheduled, so they can move on to tending or surgery. With only surgery pending, urgently hungry prisoners are still fed. Manual feeding orders still work.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerFoodDelivery_Desc: Wardens deliver food at the same hunger level as vanilla, but one trip brings enough for everyone in the cell who needs it by then, so food does not sit in the cell and spoil. Food already in the cell is counted, and only one warden delivers to a cell at a time, so wardens do not deliver twice. If a prisoner in the cell is already urgently hungry, more wardens may deliver at once to catch up, as many as the missing food needs full trips.
LanguageData.VTU_SlaveBedOwnership_Desc: A banished slave kept their slave bed after leaving, so other slaves skipped it as taken until you reassigned it by hand. The bed is now freed when a pawn stops being a slave, and beds left assigned this way in older saves are freed on load.
LanguageData.VTU_GenepackEject_Desc: Genepacks ejected from a gene bank (eject all, the eject button on a single pack, or the right-click eject in the gene assembler) get their auto-load turned off, so haulers no longer carry them straight back into a gene bank. Turn auto-load back on for a pack to let it be stored again. Genepacks dropped because a gene bank was deconstructed, uninstalled or destroyed keep auto-load on, as in vanilla.
LanguageData.VTU_PetFoodSearch: Hungry pets find food across the map
LanguageData.VTU_PetFoodSearch_Desc: A colony animal only looks for food within its nearest 100 regions, even when starving. In a large base full of doors and fences that is a small area, so a pet wandering far from the food stock could starve next to plenty of kibble. When an urgently hungry colony animal finds nothing nearby, it now searches the whole map once more (at most every 2500 ticks while nothing is found). Penned animals keep the vanilla search inside their pen.
LanguageData.VTU_TranslationFixes_Desc: Fixes mistakes in the official translations that a translation file cannot override (currently Traditional Chinese): quest text shown as "ERR:" with raw [tags] for mech cluster outposts, and generated text left in English (pilgrims quest, trial accusations, ideoligion stories, art descriptions), plus a duplicate "X and X no longer fighting" message after social fights.
LanguageData.VTU_XenogermQueue_Desc: Adds a bill-style queue to the gene assembler: do X times, until you have X, or forever. Skipping an entry keeps its progress.
LanguageData.VTU_DragReorder_Desc: Hold the right mouse button and drag to reorder the bottom bar, the architect categories and the buildings inside them.
LanguageData.VTU_MuteBirthSounds_Desc: Mutes the labor (early/late) and birth sounds. Other baby sounds are unchanged.
LanguageData.VTU_HuntGuard_Desc: When a hunter goes after an animal with any revenge chance on harm (for that hunter, at shooting range), the nearest free colonists with a ranged weapon and hostility response set to attack come along as guards: they follow the hunter and shoot anything that attacks them. There is no upper limit on guards: more are sent for an animal with more health or one with packmates close by that would join its revenge (one guard per 3 health scale: a grizzly bear is 2.5, a megasloth 3.6, a thrumbo 8). The hunter waits at the shooting spot until every guard is close, for up to 30 seconds (strict mode below gives the hunt up instead). Guards are only picked from colonists who are not hungry, tired, hurt or busy with work that cannot be interrupted, and they go back to normal work once the animal is down and no packmate that joined its revenge is still near the hunter. Hunts you order by hand are left alone.
LanguageData.VTU_HuntGuardStrict: Strict mode: give up without full guard
LanguageData.VTU_HuntGuardStrict_Desc: The hunter gives the hunt up instead of shooting without guards: when fewer guards are free than the animal needs, when a guard drops out before the first shot, or when they are not all close after 30 seconds. That hunter then leaves the animal alone for one in-game hour. Once the shooting has started, the hunt goes on even if guards leave.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerDefaultFoodPolicy: Default policies for new prisoners and slaves
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerDefaultFoodPolicy_Desc: Pawns get the food policy chosen below when they become your prisoners or slaves, and new slaves also get the apparel policy chosen below (such as Ideology's own Slave policy, whose collars and straps slow suppression loss), so these no longer have to be set by hand each time. A pawn that stops being a prisoner or slave (recruited, released, enslaved, emancipated) while still on that policy goes back to the default policy. Prisoners get no apparel policy: they never dress by one in vanilla. Policies are matched by name, so use the same names in every save.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerPolicyNoGame: Load a save to pick a policy.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerPolicyMissing: This save has no food policy named "{0}"; new prisoners keep the default policy.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerPolicyApplied: {0} prisoners now use the food policy "{1}".
LanguageData.VTU_SlavePolicyMissing: This save has no food policy named "{0}"; new slaves keep the default policy.
LanguageData.VTU_SlavePolicyApplied: {0} slaves now use the food policy "{1}".
LanguageData.VTU_SlaveApparelMissing: This save has no apparel policy named "{0}"; new slaves keep the default policy.
LanguageData.VTU_SlaveApparelApplied: {0} slaves now use the apparel policy "{1}".
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonBreak: Calmer prison breaks and slave rebellions
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonBreak_Desc: Escaping prisoners have no keys: they cannot open doors and have to break doors (or walls) to get out. Prisoners and slaves use the recreation buildings (television, chess table and so on) in the room of their own bed. Recreation calms a prisoner the way a recent break does in vanilla (about a third less likely to break out, wearing off over 5 days), so prisoners play every couple of days; it raises a slave's suppression (about 10% per session), and slaves play during recreation hours or whenever their suppression is below 30%, so a poorly suppressed slave stops working before it rebels. Instead of every prisoner in the cell, or every slave nearby, joining a break or rebellion, each one joins with a chance that drops the less inclined they are than the one who started it (recreation, a recent break, high suppression), and further with a good mood (prisoners), pain, or traits: Wimp, Nervous and Kind stay put more often, Bloodlust, Brawler and Volatile join more often. The same mood, pain and traits also make each one start a break or rebellion less (or more) often; the prisoner tab tooltip lists them. Wardens arrest a prisoner walking off the map on its own (not one in a break, those fight back), and an undrafted colonist can be ordered to arrest a prisoner that got out of its cell; the arrest can still be resisted as in vanilla. Turrets shoot prisoners in a break, inside the cell too (vanilla turrets skip all prisoners).
LanguageData.VTU_HideSlavesFromBar: Hide slaves from the colonist bar
LanguageData.VTU_HideSlavesFromBar_Desc: Slaves no longer get a portrait on the colonist bar, on maps or in caravans. Alerts such as low suppression or a slave rebellion still show and jump to them.
LanguageData.VTU_TreePractice_Desc: Pawns with a passion for Shooting or Melee can pass their recreation time practicing on a tree outside the home area and growing zones: shooting at it from a few cells away with a gun, or hitting it with a melee weapon (not with a gun or bare hands). Any tree will do, living or dead: practice never damages its target, so even strong weapons keep practicing on the same one. It counts as dexterity recreation, like horseshoes, so it helps most on maps away from the colony where nothing but meditative recreation is around. Stray shots never hit anyone; practice with a gun only happens with plain guns (no explosives, fire or single-use launchers) and only where no buildings or items (other than chunks) are within 4 cells of the tree. Special trees such as the anima tree or Gauranlen trees are left alone. Brawlers only practice with a melee weapon. Psychopaths and bloodlust pawns look for the corpses of enemies and animals first (never colonists), and shoot without caring what stray shots hit.
LanguageData.VTU_RefugeeApparel_Desc: Refugees from the hospitality quest get an apparel policy in the Assign tab and replace worn-out clothes on their own, like colonists; arriving refugees can be given a policy of your choice. The clothes they arrived in stay on until they are tattered, and anything they put on leaves with them when the quest ends. Other quest lodgers, such as guards and royal guests, still keep their own outfit.
LanguageData.VTU_RefugeeApparelMissing: This save has no apparel policy named "{0}"; refugees keep the default policy.
LanguageData.VTU_RefugeeApparelApplied: {0} refugees now use the apparel policy "{1}".
LanguageData.VTU_VisitorFood_Desc: Trader caravans, visitors and allied reinforcements, pack animals included, no longer eat food in your stockpiles or home area, or crops in growing zones and plant pots, while they carry any food of their own. Once their own food runs out and they get as hungry as the setting below, they may eat colony food again, limited to what the chosen food policy allows (animals ignore the policy). Wild food elsewhere on the map, grass included, stays open to them, so nobody starves next to your base.
LanguageData.VTU_VisitorFoodPolicyMissing: This save has no food policy named "{0}"; hungry visitors may eat any colony food.
LanguageData.VTU_HybridXenotype: Hybrid children keep a matching xenotype
LanguageData.VTU_HybridXenotype_Desc: A child labeled Hybrid whose germline genes match one heritable xenotype by more than 80% (genes weighted by complexity, skin and hair color ignored) gets that xenotype instead; a tie is decided at random. Checked at birth and on every load; genes are not changed, and pawns with xenogenes are skipped unless the option below is on.
LanguageData.VTU_HybridIncludeXenogenes_Desc: Match all genes, germline and xenogenes alike, against every xenotype (heritable or not). Also covers hybrids with xenogenes and Baseliners still shown with the default faceless icon, such as pawns implanted with a xenogerm, and checks them again right after a xenogerm is implanted. Custom xenotypes given their own icon, and mutants, are left alone.
LanguageData.VTU_FactionColors_Desc: On load, if any two factions with settlements on the world map have colors that look almost the same, the close colors are nudged apart, each moving only as far as needed and keeping its own color family as much as possible. Your own faction and the Empire keep their colors, and nothing changes when no colors are too close. The new colors are saved with the game.
LanguageData.VTU_FactionColorsMinDistance_Desc: How different two faction colors must look (OKLab distance x 100). Higher values change more factions. Takes effect on the next load.
LanguageData.VTU_CompactColonistBar_Desc: Colonist bar portraits shrink to two thirds of their height and the rows move closer together while the mouse is away and expand again when the mouse moves over the bar. Collapsed portraits show the head only.
LanguageData.VTU_RemoveFogOfWar_Desc: Reveals the whole map when it is generated or loaded. Fogged areas where revealing would set something off (sleeping enemies such as ancient dangers, quest or reveal signals, entity codex or hidden item discoveries) keep their fog and play as in vanilla; the rest of the map is still revealed. Rock, ore and collapsed rocks stay hidden until they are reached by mining, and pocket maps such as the labyrinth are never revealed.
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanFactionIcon_Desc: The form caravan, reform caravan and transport pod loading lists show the faction icon of every pawn that is not from your faction, such as guests and prisoners. Hover it for the faction name, click it for the faction info card.
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanEncounterNoJump: Caravan encounters stay on the current map
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanEncounterNoJump_Desc: When an event happens to a caravan, such as meeting another caravan, a demand from a hostile one, or a mod event like finding ruins (Real Ruins), its dialog opens without switching from the colony map to the world map. Choosing to enter the encounter map still takes you there.
LanguageData.VTU_PinnedResources: Pin resources in the resource list
LanguageData.VTU_PinnedResources_Desc: In the categorized resource list (top left), left-click a resource to pin it. Pinned resources stay listed while their category is collapsed and are shown even when you have none. Double-click to unpin. Pins apply to every save.
LanguageData.VTU_PinnedResources_Pin: Click to pin: stays listed while its category is collapsed, even at 0.
LanguageData.VTU_NutrientPasteStock_Desc: Adds a "dispense until you have X" target to nutrient paste dispensers, like a cooking bill. The number is shared by every dispenser on the map. Cooks dispense paste and drop it by the dispenser for haulers, like a bill set to drop on the floor. Paste on the ground counts toward the target as well as paste in storage, so it does not pile up before haulers arrive.
LanguageData.VTU_PS_GizmoDesc: Cooks dispense nutrient paste and drop it by the dispenser until you have this many. Shared by every dispenser on this map.
LanguageData.VTU_PS_DialogNote: Counts paste in storage, being carried and on the ground (now {0}). 0 turns it off.
LanguageData.VTU_ModUpdateNotes_Desc: The main menu's top-left box (translation credits) becomes a list of your active Steam Workshop mods, most recently updated first. Mods updated since you last opened them are highlighted; click one to read its change notes from the Workshop. An update left unopened for 3 game starts stops being highlighted. Works for every mod. On the first run every mod counts as read.
LanguageData.VTU_MU_Failed: Could not load the change notes. Use the button above to open the page.
LanguageData.VTU_MU_NoNotes: The Workshop change notes page has no entry for this version.
LanguageData.VTU_BreakUpFights_Desc: Anyone who sees a social fight nearby and is not hostile to either fighter (colonists, visitors, even raiders among themselves) may step in and try to stop it, unless they are busy with work that cannot be interrupted. A rival of either fighter, or anyone with Bloodlust, may instead join in against the fighter they like least. Success depends on their Social skill and on how much the fighters like them. When it fails, the fighter may turn on them, using the vanilla social fight formula, and the old opponent keeps going: a brawl that lasts until that fighter stops. Anyone hit by someone they are not fighting back may turn on them, so a brawl can split into several fights. Fighters remember who broke up their fight: most are grateful, but some resent it. Mood matters too: pawns in a bad mood insult others more often, start or join fights more readily, are harder to calm down and less willing to step in; a good mood works the other way (from x1.5 at 20% mood to x0.7 at 90%).
LanguageData.VTU_BF_JoinedIn: {PAWN1_labelShort} jumped into the fight to gang up on {PAWN2_labelShort}!
LanguageData.VTU_BF_DraggedIn: {PAWN1_labelShort} turned on {PAWN2_labelShort}, who tried to break up the fight!
LanguageData.VTU_ShortMapNames_Desc: Names under pawns on the map are cut to about one and a half cells wide (following the zoom) so long names do not cover their neighbours. The full name shows while the mouse is over the pawn or its name, or while the pawn is selected.
LanguageData.VTU_GhoulApparel_Desc: Ghouls keep their clothes when turned and can be ordered to wear clothes and armor (right-click the apparel with the ghoul selected). They never change clothes on their own and still cannot use weapons.
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanAbandonDead: Caravan: abandon all dead at once
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanAbandonDead_Desc: Adds a button next to "Assign drug policies" on the caravan Items tab that abandons every human corpse and every tainted apparel (worn by someone who died) in the caravan inventory after one confirmation. Animal corpses are kept for butchering. Dead colonists are named in the confirmation. Apparel worn by living members is not touched.
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanAbandonDead_Tip: Abandon every human corpse and every tainted apparel in this caravan's inventory. Animal corpses are kept.
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanAbandonDead_Confirm: Abandon {0} human corpse(s) and {1} tainted apparel?
LanguageData.VTU_CaravanAbandonDead_Colonists: This includes the bodies of these colonists:
LanguageData.VTU_TaskbarLetterBadge_Desc: Shows the letters waiting on the right side of the screen as a small badge over the game's taskbar button: their number, coloured like the most urgent one (red for big threats, orange for small threats, and so on). Opening or dismissing letters updates it. While a critical (red) alert is active, such as a life-threatening condition or a colonist needing rescue, the badge turns red too, or shows a plain red dot when there are no letters. With no letters, a message on the top left shows a plain dot in the matching colour for as long as it stays on screen. While the game is paused the number becomes a pause sign (the colour stays), on a grey badge when there is nothing else to show. A glance at the taskbar tells you something happened while you were in another window. No pop-ups, sounds or flashing. Windows only.
LanguageData.VTU_BundleLetterDismiss_Desc: When too many letters pile up, the oldest ones are folded into a single "N more..." letter that ignores right-click. Right-clicking it now dismisses all the letters inside at once, like right-clicking a normal letter. Letters that still wait for your choice (such as someone asking to join or visitors at the gate) cannot be dismissed with a right click and stay.
LanguageData.VTU_VisitorShelter: Visitors take shelter from bad weather and enemies
LanguageData.VTU_VisitorShelter_Desc: Trader caravans and visitor groups wait just outside the colony and leave early as soon as any member, pack animals included, starts getting hypothermia or heatstroke. When the temperature at their spot gets close to the limit of the most sensitive member, or enemies of some strength are active on the map (a single hunted animal fighting back does not count), they move into a barn if they brought animals, otherwise a dining room, with a storeroom as the fallback for both. The room must be at a safe temperature and reachable by all of them. While sheltering they eat inside too: they sit at a table in the room or eat standing there, and only fetch food from outside the room once urgently hungry. Rain at their spot also sends them inside, quietly, and so does night (22:00 to 6:00) so they sleep indoors, though only in a barn or storeroom, never on a dining room floor. They go back outside once the enemies, the rain and the night are gone and the weather is mild again. Checked every few in-game minutes, also while they are still walking in (they then head straight for the room); a group that is already too cold or hot by then still leaves, and guards still fight enemies that come near.
LanguageData.VTU_VisitorShelter_Moved: Because of {1}, {0} moved into the {2} for now.
LanguageData.VTU_ConfirmCloseWindow: Confirm before closing the game window
LanguageData.VTU_ConfirmCloseWindow_Desc: Closing the game window (the X button or Alt+F4) during a game quits at once. It now goes through the same steps as Quit to OS in the in-game menu: if there is unsaved progress you are asked to confirm first, and in commitment mode the game is saved before it quits. On the main menu the window still closes right away.
LanguageData.VTU_SlavePrisonerBeds_Desc: Slaves can sleep and recover in prisoner beds, medical ones included, so they can share the prison wing instead of needing their own bedrooms and hospital. A prisoner you enslave keeps the bed in their cell.
LanguageData.VTU_PrisonerHelpers_Desc: Kind prisoners tend cellmates lying in bed (always without medicine, so the quality is low; doctors still tend as usual) and feed bedridden cellmates who are left very hungry (wardens usually come first) from food or a nutrient paste dispenser in the cell. Hard-working, industrious or neurotic prisoners clean their cell when they have nothing else to do, unless they are also lazy. Only prisoners with these traits do it, and only inside their own cell.
LanguageData.VTU_InspectTabCamera: Camera jumps avoid the open inspect tab
LanguageData.VTU_InspectTabCamera_Desc: Jumping the camera to a colonist (the next/previous colonist keys, double-clicking a portrait on the colonist bar, letters) puts it in the middle of the screen, where an open inspect tab (log, gear, social, character, needs, health) covers the left part. While such a tab is open, the colonist is now centred in the uncovered part of the screen to the right of the tab. Only the horizontal position changes.
LanguageData.VTU_InspectTabCameraOnOpen: Also move the camera when a tab opens over the selected pawn
LanguageData.VTU_InspectTabCameraOnOpen_Desc: When you open or switch to a tab that covers the selected pawn, the camera slides sideways so the pawn shows to the right of the tab. Nothing moves if the pawn is already visible, or when the tab closes.
LanguageData.VTU_FieldTending_Desc: A downed colonist or prisoner lying outside a bed is tended where they lie if they would bleed to death within 6 hours, or if no bed is free for them. A fast bleeder tended this way gets only medicine the doctor carries, or none, so nobody walks to a stockpile first. Better medicine only lowers a wound's infection chance and speeds its healing; it does not stop bleeding any better. So patients with no untended wound that can get infected and no disease that can kill get the cheapest medicine their medical care setting allows. Wounds that can get infected (cuts, bites, gunshots, burns, frostbite) and deadly diseases (infection, flu, plague, carcinoma and the like) still get the best, even between that disease's own tends.
LanguageData.VTU_FieldTendBeforeCapture: Tend fast bleeders before capturing them
LanguageData.VTU_FieldTendBeforeCapture_Desc: A colonist told to capture or arrest a downed pawn who would bleed to death within 6 hours tends them where they lie first (with carried medicine, or none), then carries them off. They are taken prisoner as the tend begins, so they cannot get up as an enemy mid-tend.
LanguageData.VTU_Quicksave_Desc: Press F5 during play to save right away, without opening the menu. Saves are named Quicksave-1, Quicksave-2 and so on; once all of them exist, the oldest one is overwritten, the same way autosaves rotate. Pressing again before any game time has passed (for example while paused) overwrites the same file instead. The key can be changed in Options > Keyboard (Game section). In commitment mode the game's single save file is used, like autosave. The "Really quit?" confirmation gets a "Save and quit" button that quicksaves first. The main menu gets a Continue button at the top that loads your newest save (autosaves and quicksaves included), with the usual version and mod list warnings; hover it to see which save it loads, or press Enter on the main menu to do the same (key changeable in Options > Keyboard).
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_AddToQueueDesc: Add this xenogerm to the assembler's queue instead of replacing the current job. Queued xenogerms start automatically one after another, like workbench bills.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_QueueGizmoDesc: View and edit the queue of xenogerms this assembler will create automatically.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_PausedHint: Queue is paused. No new xenogerm will be started until it is resumed.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_Empty: The queue is empty. Use "Add to queue" in the recombine window.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_SkipDesc: Set this xenogerm aside and start the next entry in the queue. Its progress is kept and continues when it comes up again. Inserted archite capsules are dropped next to the assembler.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_SkipNoNext: No other queue entry can be started right now.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_DeleteRunningDesc: Remove from queue. The xenogerm in progress is not cancelled.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_MissingGenepacks: Xenogerm queue: skipping {0}, some genepacks are no longer in a connected gene bank.
LanguageData.VTU_XQ_QueuePaused: Xenogerm queue paused because the current xenogerm was cancelled.
LanguageData.VTU_DR_Hint: Hold the right mouse button on a bottom bar button, an architect category, a building or a command button of the selection, drag it onto another one and release to move it there. Command buttons share one order across pawns, buildings and animals.
LanguageData.VTU_DR_ResetDesignators: Reset building order in all categories
LanguageData.VTU_CB_ShowIcons: Status icons (sleeping, idle, mental break, role...)
LanguageData.VTU_CB_ShowWeapons: Weapons (when shown under portraits in the game options)
LanguageData.VTU_CB_MagnifyHovered: Enlarge the portrait under the mouse
LanguageData.VTU_CB_MagnifyHovered_Desc: The entry under the mouse becomes a bit wider and its portrait a bit larger; the head stays in view and the feet are cut off. Clicks in the gap next to a portrait also go to that portrait.
LanguageData.VTU_CB_CustomPortraits_Desc: Makes colonist bar entries taller and moves the portrait camera closer, so each entry shows the whole pawn inside its frame. Off: vanilla size.
LanguageData.VTU_CB_PortraitsByCustomPortraits: Portrait size is controlled by [NL] Custom Portraits while it is active.
LanguageData.VTU_CB_RaceZoom: Extra zoom per race (races on the colonist bar):
